class.name: DampedSpring2D
class.brief_description: A damped spring that smooths a [Vector2] value toward a target.
class.description:
A spring instance. You should create and update one spring instance for each value you wish to smooth.
See also [DampedSpring] and [DampedSpring3D] for the [float]/[Vector3] equivalents.

method.name: update
method.description:
Updates the spring inertia state, and returns a new value.
Call this once per frame (or physics tick), passing in the value returned by the previous call as [param value]. If [param parameters] is [code]null[/code], [member velocity] is left unchanged and [param value] is returned as-is.

method.name: update_blend
method.description: Like [method update], but blends smoothly between two [DampedSpringParameters] tunings instead of using just one: the spring/damping constants used for this step are linearly interpolated between [param parameters_a] and [param parameters_b] by [param weight] ([code]0.0[/code] = fully [param parameters_a], [code]1.0[/code] = fully [param parameters_b]). Useful for crossfading between two "feels" (e.g. a relaxed and a snappy tuning) over time, rather than jumping between them. If either [param parameters_a] or [param parameters_b] is [code]null[/code], [member velocity] is left unchanged and [param value] is returned as-is.

method.name: update_constants
method.description:
Like [method update], but takes the spring's [param spring_constant]/[param damping_constant] coefficients directly instead of a [DampedSpringParameters] resource -- e.g. [member DampedSpringParameters.spring_constant]/[member DampedSpringParameters.damping_constant], or values computed/blended by the caller.
This method is added for advanced manual spring blending use cases, or if you wish to specify damped spring parameters in a different way.

members.member: The spring's current rate of change, advanced in place by [method update]. Usually left for [method update] to manage; can be read or set directly to inspect the spring's momentum, reset it, or give it an initial velocity.
